gaps_vs_goal: Autonomous target derivation: the entire dynamic-evidence chain (harness generation -> PropertyCorpus -> Echidna/Medusa/Halmos/Kontrol -> forge invariants -> fork PoC) is keyed on config.reproduction.targets, a human-supplied map of contract name -> literal deployed address (invariant_templates.py:87-92, reproduction.py:1121-1137). For SYNTHETIC_BENCHMARK corpora (no deployment) nothing derives targets from the source or a local deployment plan, so every engine SKIPs. The goal's 'no human blocker' is violated at the first step of evidence generation; the inventory itself marks gate-reproduction-target-derivation MISSING.

Engine provisioning: no code in this subsystem or in the managed toolchain fetches, pins, or verifies echidna/medusa/halmos/z3/kontrol; adapters demand operator version+sha256 pins and otherwise return INCONCLUSIVE/UNAVAILABLE. A fully automated auditor needs a hash-pinned toolchain bundle acquired and verified without an operator.

Local deployment synthesis: the translation subset only supports contracts with an argument-less constructor, one target, no token seeding, no ETH value, no time travel, no ordering (engines/echidna.py:224-246). Real protocols (vaults, lending, AMMs) need constructor args, multi-contract wiring, token minting and warp/roll; the FoundryInvariantRunner has a local_deployments mechanism (config LocalInvariantDeployment) but it is again operator-authored config, not derived.

Exploit expressiveness: the PoC DSL cannot deploy attacker contracts, receive callbacks, take flash loans, sign messages, or pass arrays/structs (schemas.py:1797-1802; reproduction.py:1379-1517). Reentrancy, flash-loan price manipulation, callback-based and signature-replay exploits — the majority of high-severity DeFi findings — cannot be reproduced, so they can never earn CONFIRMED status through execution.

Cross-lineage engine judgement: only echidna-vs-medusa disagreement is computed (formal.py:2283); there is no adjudication combining symbolic (halmos/kontrol/SMTChecker) with fuzzing results or with model candidates, so engine evidence cannot serve as the goal's 'different root_lineage' judge of model findings.

Linux/CI execution parity: the CI backend (bubblewrap) cannot reach a loopback fork RPC (reproduction.py:303), so fork-based PoC and non-local invariant execution are impossible on the reference platform without operator-declared offline fork archives (gate-fork-environment CURRENT_MANUAL_INPUT). Synthetic-corpus runs would need a fully local deployment path that does not require any fork at all.

Certora is structurally incompatible with the goal (remote paid service, operator-authored CVL, API key, network egress) and should be either dropped or replaced by local proof tooling; it currently contributes only config surface.

Compilation and formal execution are off by default and enabled only through the maximum-assurance profile; a best-in-world auditor should compile and run at least SMTChecker/foundry invariants on every audit, with the profile controlling depth not existence.

Evidence that any engine has ever produced a real SUCCESS in this repo is absent (runtime_status.json:996-1004 all false; no run artifact found); the subsystem's correctness against real Echidna/Halmos/Medusa/Kontrol output formats is validated only against hand-written canned JSON in unit tests.

Project handling gaps that will break real corpora: foundry.toml src/libs/test overrides and non-default profiles ignored (projects.py:31, 274), no forge-style auto remapping from lib/, Hardhat config parsed by regex, Mythril only analyses one file (formal.py:359).

NOT collapsed (they escape the handler because they are BaseException): asyncio.CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit - re-raised by the runner at development_corpus_ensemble.py:602,607 and propagated raw to Typer; only repeat-manifest catches CancelledError explicitly (development_cli.py:794-800). Practical effect: a missing ledger file, a wrong reviewer model alias, a pre-existing output directory, a corrupt endpoint snapshot, a 2 MB sources.json overflow and an internal bug all print the identical sentence and exit code, and the user has no stack trace.

Sub-child failures are double-collapsed: inside run_development_corpus the shard loop's `except Exception: reason = "LOCAL_FAILURE"` (development_corpus.py:443-444) records no exception type or message anywhere in result.json (DevelopmentCorpusObservation has only stop_reason), so a LOCAL_FAILURE caused by a custody check versus a pydantic bug in response decoding is unrecoverable from the artifacts; same at development_corpus_judgment.py:470-471, development_corpus_ensemble.py:558-559, development_corpus_repeats.py:477-478, development_corpus_resume.py:598-599, development_ensemble.py:388-389. development_transport.py:735-740 also swallows all telemetry-projection exceptions.

Byte-bound mismatch between producer and consumer: run_development_corpus writes sources.json with max_bytes=MAX_DEVELOPMENT_CORPUS_RESULT_BYTES (64,000,000; development_corpus.py:357,220) and a manifest may carry up to MAX_DEVELOPMENT_CORPUS_BYTES=8,388,608 source bytes (models/development_corpus.py:62), but judge-manifest reads sources.json with max_bytes=2_000_000 (development_cli.py:612-616,657) - so a candidate produced by audit-manifest over a >~2 MB corpus cannot be judged standalone, though ensemble-manifest handles the same corpus in-process.

I ran tests/integration/test_development_corpus_ensemble_cli.py, ..._execution.py and test_development_ensemble_cli.py: 78 passed in 272s. Not tested anywhere I could find: a real OpenRouter round trip, a real ledger reconciliation against a provider-reported cost, and any exercise of the collapsed-exception paths asserting which underlying error occurred (tests assert only exit code and the fixed refusal text).
gaps_vs_goal: No root-lineage predicate: reviewer distinctness is by model-id string only (models/development_ensemble.py:71-79); the frozen goal's 'judged only by a different root_lineage; same-root judgement voids it' has no data field, no check, and no way to express it (lineage_independence is a single-value Literal). Two OpenRouter aliases of the same underlying provider family would pass.

No externally-anchored seal: nothing in this subsystem publishes any hash to a transparency log or produces an inclusion proof; result.json/score.json are private local files whose only integrity is an in-process sha256.

No hash-pinned-corpus authority: truth files are optional (--truth-manifest) and provenance is not checked; the corpora that are pinned by hash (DEVELOPMENT_AUDIT_SOURCE_PINS) are two 3-file synthetic fixtures (models/development_audit.py:39-60). There is no wired path from a public benchmark corpus with known findings into ensemble-manifest other than the operator hand-authoring a manifest and a truth JSON.

Human blockers remain in every run: each paid command requires the operator to pass --accept-estimate-risk and --allow-code-egress (development_cli.py:1047-1053), to pre-provision the ledger (open_existing only, :1153), to hand-select three endpoint snapshot files, and to invoke each stage (audit -> judge, or repeat, or resume) as a separate command; resume is explicitly manual (development_corpus_resume.py:435-438). There is no orchestrator that chains these into an unattended campaign.

Run halts on first failure with no recovery inside the run: one 429 or one timeout on file k aborts files k+1..n (development_corpus.py:437-439) and the whole ensemble reports INCOMPLETE; for a 'no human blocker' run this means any transient provider error ends the audit and requires an operator to run resume-manifest.

Budget is an estimate, not a ceiling: preflight compares plan estimates to ledger remaining (development_corpus_ensemble.py:415) and docstrings concede budgets 'can be exceeded'; there is no abort-at-ceiling mid-run other than the per-request reservation logic in the transport, and the CLI requires acknowledging overspend risk.

Scale bounds: 256 files, 262,144 bytes per file, 8 MiB total (models/development_corpus.py:59-62), sequential single-threaded requests, and a 1,800 s whole-run cap (development_cli.py:1022-1024) - a realistic protocol with hundreds of files and a 4-minute model latency cannot complete inside one invocation.

Consensus is descriptive only: SUPPORTED/REFUTED/INCONCLUSIVE strings from two opinions (models/development_corpus_ensemble.py:271-273) with no adjudication over frozen ground truth and no cross-examination stage; the goal's 'all adjudication cross-lineage automated over the frozen corpus' has no counterpart here.

Diagnosability for an autonomous supervisor is poor: every failure class collapses to one sentence and ExitCode.CONFIGURATION at the CLI, and to stop_reason=LOCAL_FAILURE with no message in result.json, so an automated controller cannot distinguish 'ledger missing' from 'output dir exists' from 'reviewer alias collision' from 'internal bug' without a human reading the retained files.

purpose: Everything between the engine and OpenRouter: an httpx client that sends structured-output chat completions with an explicit provider allowlist and price cap, validates the returned identity (model, provider endpoint, router strategy, generation ID), retries transient failures on the same route, fetches /api/v1/generation for cost/token reconciliation, and records a UsageRecord for budget accounting. Around that: fail-closed validation of per-model endpoint metadata (pricing, capabilities, ZDR, reasoning support), a closed inventory of 31 route-admission predicates, per-role reasoning-effort policy, operator-authored candidate-selection plans (which models/endpoints may be discovered and in which candidate/judge roles), and atomic storage of benchmark reports. It is the mechanism by which the product goal's 'exact model identity' and '$250 ceiling' are supposed to be enforced per call.

Model and route selection is a human step: the selection plan is operator-authored (artifact_kind OPERATOR_STAGED_MODEL_SELECTION, candidate_selection.py:982-985), all authorization flags are Literal[False], and the candidate/judge triple is compiled into validators (:724-738). Cross-lineage independence — the goal's authority requirement — is never verified or even representable as true in this subsystem (distinct_root_lineages_verified Literal[False], root_lineage=None at candidate_selection.py:230/:4199). A world-class autonomous auditor needs a lineage collision map enforced at route-admission time.

No resilience beyond same-route retry: no provider rotation on 429/5xx, no per-model multi-endpoint policy in the audit path (runtime.py:71-77), and the development transport refuses to retry at all (development_transport.py:608-651). A fully automated run at $250 with 12 candidate models will stall on the first sustained rate limit instead of routing around it.

No response-quality/engagement gate: empty findings are explicitly allowed by prompt (development_review.py:64) and no code detects a disengaged model; only the surface-set schema (schemas.py:3538-3572) forces per-surface records. An autonomous auditor must detect and re-dispatch low-engagement responses (e.g. all surfaces REVIEWED_NO_ISSUE with boilerplate rationale, zero reasoning tokens when reasoning was requested).

Same-model-different-provider variance (quantization fp4/fp8, different serving stacks) is neither measured nor reconciled; the design pins one endpoint per model, so a provider-specific regression is invisible and unrecoverable without a new operator plan.

purpose: Deterministic, non-model tool execution layer of the Corrovera/mmaudit audit pipeline. It (a) wraps fixed-argument static/secret/dependency scanners (semgrep, gitleaks, trivy, osv-scanner, codeql, slither) in a copied disposable workspace under a hardened isolation backend (sandbox-exec on macOS / bubblewrap on Linux / rootless container), pins tool identity by version+SHA-256, and normalizes machine output into ScannerFinding records that feed the model context and the maximum-assurance contract; (b) runs the repository's own Foundry fork test suite (forge test / forge coverage --report debug / forge test --debug --dump / forge test --list) against a loopback pinned-fork RPC, with inventory, statement-coverage and debugger evidence; (c) supplies a read-only RPC bridge, a clean-Anvil launcher for fork-matrix differentials, and an offline recorded-RPC replay service; (d) contains a fully fail-closed Hardhat stub that never executes target JavaScript.

design_observations: One-shot-per-ledger request identity: full-campaign candidate ids are `authrunner.candidate.{primary|replay}:{case_id}` with no model or run salt (src/mmaudit/benchmark/models.py:703-705) and judge ids `cross-lineage-{request_sha256}` (benchmark/cross_lineage_adjudication.py:745); the ledger rejects any repeated request_id (cost_ledger.py:530-531). A second campaign on the same cumulative ledger - a retry after failure, or a different candidate - fails at its first reservation. Only the smoke path carries a run index. No test covers a re-run.

A single transient provider failure is fatal AND permanently poisons the ledger: 429/timeout -> UNCERTAIN_ACCOUNTED at full reservation (openrouter.py:19959-19965, cost_ledger.py:952-967) -> next reserve refused by require_known_prior_costs (budgets.py:3668-3676, cost_ledger.py:541-546) -> interval close would also refuse (authenticated_runner_ledger.py:494-503). This already happened twice in smoke (runtime_status.json:2127 smoke_r2 uncertain_accounted, 2142 smoke_r17 operator timeout) and was resolved by a hand-authored hardcoded allowance (legacy_cost_allowance.py:44-96). Docs describe this as the OP-COST 'unknown billing blocks new work' feature; the code makes it a human gate.

RESERVED-row blocking is mode dependent: plain reserve() only subtracts active reservations from remaining (cost_ledger.py:1859-1868); require_settled_prior_costs (dev path only, development_budget.py:119) refuses on any RESERVED row or held portfolio (cost_ledger.py:548-563); the AUTHRUNNER preflight refuses launch if active_reserved_usd != 0 or any RESERVED entry exists (models/authenticated_runner_execution.py:2020-2040) and there is no CLI to clear one.

Whole-run 'second cap' is arithmetic at preflight only (declared_final_spent_cap_usd < 250, authenticated_runner_execution.py:1489-1494) plus a judge-stage recheck (896-903); there is no running accumulator against declared_interval_cost_cap_usd. Enforcement during the run is per-attempt ceiling (budgets.py:2119) and the ledger's 250 cap.

AUTHRUNNER requires a strictly serial request stream despite config concurrency=3: any in-flight UNCERTAIN_ACCOUNTED row blocks the next reservation under require_known_prior_costs; benchmark/models.py:1543-1551 and cross_lineage_adjudication.py:1551 loop cases sequentially, so it works, but the invariant is implicit.

gaps_vs_goal: No unattended entry point: the qualified campaign needs an operator to run three fresh discovery commands, build three singleton registries, produce a smoke bundle, pick three per-attempt cost caps, supply a secrets file and an initialized ledger, then invoke `models authenticated-runner` (cli.py:2507-2620); gate-managed-completion-entrypoint is MISSING and gate-authenticated-real-campaign is CURRENT_MANUAL_INPUT in docs/remediation/v3/autonomy_gate_inventory.json.

Zero-human-blocker budget handling is violated by design: the goal says 'abort at ceiling, never ask; per-call reconciliation recorded', but any provider transient (429, 5xx, timeout, missing cost in response) turns into an UNCERTAIN_ACCOUNTED row that (a) aborts the run, (b) blocks every future reservation under the operator policy, and (c) can only be cleared by editing a hardcoded two-row allowance in code (legacy_cost_allowance.py:44-96) plus emitting a new hash-pinned selection plan. An autonomous auditor needs generation-id backed settlement (fetch /generation?id= and reconcile to known cost) or bounded conservative carry, wired into the runner.

Unsalted request identity means the $250 cumulative ledger can host exactly one full-campaign attempt (benchmark/models.py:703-705, cost_ledger.py:530-531); a failed run cannot be retried without a new ledger file, which resets the spend accounting the ledger exists to protect (cost_ledger.py:346-354 docstring).

No external append-only anchoring of the runner seal: the 'transparency proof' is a locally computed Merkle prefix (evidence_seal_authority.py:1469-1526); the OpenTimestamps calendar client and calibration checkpoint publication exist but are reachable only from tests; the runner's AUTHSEAL outputs are declared nonauthorizing and every authority flag is a hardcoded False (1546-1556). Goal item 2 (published to a transparency log, verified by independent re-run + inclusion proof) has no code path.

Judge-stage spend is admitted only after both candidate passes have been paid for (authenticated_runner_execution.py:870-910); preflight cannot bound the full campaign (inventory constant PENDING_REAL_CANDIDATE_OUTPUTS at 1564), so an operator cannot know before spending whether the judge stage fits under the tripwires.

Configured transient retry (max_model_retries=1) is dead under the operator policy (test_operator_reservation_transport.py:218-280 documents 'forbids retry'); a real 96-request campaign against public providers with no effective transient retry has a low probability of finishing, and schema retries need a separate byte-pinned config.

The three AUTHRUNNER routes in config/models.selection-plan.json are NONAUTHORIZING with discovery_evidence_present=false and 13 unresolved requirements; nothing in this subsystem can advance that state without operator-run discovery.

No end-to-end test of the qualified path through a mock transport, no test of ledger reuse across campaigns, and no test of the retained/calibration scope from a user-runnable command; the confidence in the docs is not backed by a full-path test.

Development path (the only path that has spent money on real audits) is explicitly non-qualifying, single-attempt everywhere (maximum_attempts != 1 rejected in nine modules), and cannot feed the authority chain; the qualified path has never completed (runtime_status.json completed_real_audits=0, superiority_status=NOT_DEMONSTRATED, global ledger $0.68 spent over 57 smoke/dev entries).

Recovery tooling is absent for the AUTHRUNNER ledger: no CLI to release a stale RESERVED row, settle an uncertain row, or inspect the ledger; the scheduler's recovery (scheduler.py:8270-8420) only serves `mmaudit run` journals.

subsystem: tests/ (pytest suite for the mmaudit/Corrovera engine)
purpose: The test suite is the only executable evidence that the engine's fail-closed invariants hold: that mock/synthetic provider traffic can never be relabelled as REAL execution evidence, that cross-lineage/ground-truth/seal authority objects cannot be forged, copied, pickled or minted by a caller, that budgets/ledgers refuse overspend, and that the governance documents in docs/remediation/v3 stay internally consistent. It is not, and by its own docstrings does not claim to be, evidence that the auditor finds vulnerabilities, completes an audit, or produces an externally anchored seal. In the product's own terms, it proves the refusal surface, not the audit surface.
